fieldValues.title: The three sibling container-question units predate their own ruling
fieldValues.summary: programme units 57825db9 (srs#572), 08faf3eb (srs#573) and 65c41ce6 (srs#574) still read lifecycleState: proposed and decision_mode: complex, and 57825db9's summary still says RFC-034 stays deferred. All three were actually dispositioned together with srs#267 by rfc-decision-0750c62f (PR #610, merged 2026-09-06) per that PR's own comment on srs#580 ("#572, #573, #574 each dispositioned as a consequence of the plane assignment rather than argued separately"). A worker picking up any of the three should re-derive it against rfc-decision-0750c62f rather than trust the stored mode/summary, per the revival rule (CLAUDE.md) applied to stale unit records rather than a stale branch.
fieldValues.rationale: These three units were authored 2026-09-05 (srs#583/#593) before rfc-decision-0750c62f existed (ruled 2026-09-06). Nothing re-synced them when the ruling landed, because the ruling's own PR (#610) touched srs/records/ (the decision record) and docs/charter/decision-compass.md, not programme/records/ (a different repository's data). This unit (RFC-034 Rev 5 execution, PR #616) only touched its own unit record and did not update the three siblings, since doing so was outside srs#267's dispatch scope and the coordinator, not an individual worker, owns re-syncing sibling units. What would change this: the coordinator or a dedicated unit walks 57825db9/08faf3eb/65c41ce6, re-runs Classify/Charter against rfc-decision-0750c62f, and either transitions them to landed (if fully absorbed, as #572's membership question appears to be) or rewrites their summary/decision_mode to reflect what the ruling actually left open, if anything.
